results.claim: The source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm’s complexity is Θ(n+M_FIFO), where M_FIFO=Σ_t|Q_t| for its actual marked queues; processing (p_t,Q_t) yields p_{t+1}=reverse(Q_t) followed by the stable deletion of Q_t from p_t.
results.proof_sketch: Initialization costs Θ(n). Every subsequent PopFront/MoveToFront performs a constant number of list, queue, and comparison operations, so the remaining cost is Θ(Σ_t|Q_t|). Moving the distinct elements of Q_t to the front in FIFO order reverses their order and preserves the relative order of all other elements. Although Q_0 lists the initial descent bottoms from left to right, later queues are ordered by detection events during earlier moves. For p=(4,1,5,2,6,3), the first shelf state is (3,2,1,4,5,6), but Q_1=(1,2), while the shelf-order descent-bottom list is (2,1). Thus the literal next shelf is (2,1,3,4,5,6), not reverse(D(p_1)) followed by U(p_1).

results.claim: There is an exact phase decomposition that isolates the unresolved cost.
results.proof_sketch: Let i be the largest unfixed value and s_i<i its position when its phase starts. All larger values form a permanent fixed suffix, so i is not a descent bottom. Before a round, partition its marked elements into ℓ_t elements left of i and q_t elements right of i. Removing and then prepending an element left of i shifts i once left and once right, for net zero; prepending an element removed from its right shifts i right exactly once. Hence its position increases by q_t, independently of FIFO order. When i reaches position i, Σ_t q_t=i−s_i. The phase move count is therefore exactly (i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t. Bounding the accumulated left-of-active moves remains the unresolved part.

results.claim: The parent does not establish an Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound, or the coefficient (4√2/3+o(1)), for the source-literal optimized FIFO algorithm.

It does not describe later FIFO queues of the literal optimized pseudocode. Consequently the claimed prefix identity and its summation do not count the requested execution. This withdraws the proposed proof; it does not assert that an Ω(n^{3/2}) bound is false.

results.claim: A natural twice-per-unordered-pair charging bound is false.
results.proof_sketch: For p=(2,4,…,4096,1,3,…,4095), exact literal FIFO execution makes 49,545,006 moves. This exceeds 2·binom(4096,2)=16,773,120, so a charging invariant allowing at most two moves per unordered pair cannot cover every execution. The earlier counts 161 for P_13 and 50,546,772 for this instance belong to the ordinary T process and are removed; literal P_13 makes 97 moves. final_writeup:
Partial progress, but not a solution of the target, is claimed. The revision preserves the exact parent’s corrected model of the source-literal optimized FIFO pseudocode.

Let Q_t be the optimized algorithm’s actual FIFO queue at the beginning of round t. Processing Q_t changes the shelf p_t to reverse(Q_t) followed by the elements outside Q_t in their previous relative order. The initial queue is the left-to-right list of descent bottoms, but subsequent queues are appended in the order that new marks are detected while earlier elements are removed and prepended. That order need not be shelf order. Thus the correct evolving state is (p_t,Q_t), and the running time is Θ(n+Σ_t|Q_t|), rather than a weighted orbit under T(p)=reverse(D(p))·U(p).

The distinction is visible on (4,1,5,2,6,3). After round one the shelf is (3,2,1,4,5,6), while the literal next queue is (1,2). Literal FIFO processing therefore produces (2,1,3,4,5,6); processing the current descent bottoms in shelf order would instead produce the sorted permutation. Literal execution takes six moves in three rounds, versus five moves in two ordinary-T rounds.

There is also an exact phase decomposition. If i is the largest unfixed value and its phase begins at position s_i, all larger values form a permanent fixed suffix and i cannot be marked. In any round, a moved element initially left of i has zero net effect on i’s position, while one initially right of i advances i by one. If ℓ_t and q_t are the respective counts, then Σ_tq_t=i−s_i and the phase makes exactly

(i−s_i)+Σ_tℓ_t

moves. Controlling the second term remains the obstacle.

The proposed Ω(n^{3/2}) lower bound remains withdrawn. Its staircase calculation applies only to the auxiliary ordinary transition and was not transferred to the literal FIFO process. Already for P_6, their states differ after three rounds. This invalidates the proposed proof and coefficient without proving that such a lower bound is impossible.

Exact exhaustive literal execution gives move maxima 0,1,3,6,11,18,27,38,53 for n=1,…,9. The corrected even-then-odd instance of size 4096 makes 49,545,006 moves, exceeding 2·binom(4096,2)=16,773,120 and thereby refuting a twice-per-unordered-pair charging invariant. It is only a finite obstruction and establishes no asymptotic lower bound.

Accordingly, neither a stronger asymptotic lower bound nor a better upper bound has been proved. The requested tight complexity remains open between the authorized source’s Ω(n log n) and O(n³) bounds. Nevertheless, the corrected state model, exact phase identity, exhaustive small-n maxima, and obstruction to one charging argument are material progress directly relevant to the target; claimed_resolution is therefore PARTIAL.
